sources.entry: Archcore - Git-native context engineering and spec-driven development for AI coding agents. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: Archcore is a Git-native system that keeps specs, decisions, rules, plans, and guides as Markdown in a .archcore/ folder so AI coding agents can read project context before making changes.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a CLI plus agent plugins that let an AI coding agent create and use typed project documents stored in the repo under .archcore/. The /archcore:init command reads the repo and proposes documents for the stack, how to run the project, and an architecture overview. /archcore:plan reads existing documents and creates a spec, examples in Given/When/Then form, and tasks, sized to the change. /archcore:document turns one sentence into a linked document such as a decision, rule, module description, or how-to, with a status of draft or accepted. /archcore:review compares a branch against the documents in both directions and labels each finding as code-wrong or spec-wrong. It can also import existing CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or rule files into typed documents.
use_cases: give AI coding agents persistent project context
record architectural decisions in the repo
plan a feature with a spec and tasks before coding
review a branch against documented rules before merge
import existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md files into structured docs
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (macOS, Linux, or WSL; the URL was stripped from the README)
irm | iex  (Windows PowerShell 5.1+; the URL was stripped from the README)
notable: Stores specs, decisions, rules, plans, and guides as versioned Markdown files in the repo, so changes appear as pull request diffs
Typed documents identified by filename suffix, such as .spec.md, .plan.md, .adr.md, and .rule.md
/archcore:review checks code against documents in both directions and assigns a verdict to each finding
Imports existing CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and rule files into typed documents
caveats: The README says a small fix gets no documents, so the tool adds little to projects that only make small fixes
Documents must be reviewed and kept current by the team, which is a real ongoing cost
Cursor requires one extra setup step; OpenCode setup differs by command syntax
The README says a single CLAUDE.md is still enough for a small repo with few rules
